reason: The draft answers the question the right way. It says plainly not to go to 80 miles with doubles and gives honest reasons: fitness takes time to arrive, the club mate built up over years, and doubles don't suit marathon training. The plan adds up to 45 mi (6+9+9+4+17). That's a sensible step after 40 this week, and below the 53-mile spike two weeks ago. The long run goes from 15 to 17 mi, a modest rise. The plan keeps Marisol's schedule: Monday and Friday off, the session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday. Each day has a distance, a heart-rate cap or a pace, so it can be run as written. The paces fit her goal: 7:55–8:05/mi for the 1.5-mile repeats is quicker than 3:45 marathon pace (about 8:35/mi), which suits this kind of session, and 9:50–10:05/mi is a fair easy pace for the long run. Her heavy legs cleared by Thursday, so this isn't an injury or exhaustion flag. I marked it down slightly because some lines go beyond what the card shows. "Ran this week exactly as planned" isn't on the card. "You have already seen what a big jump costs" stretches a mild report of heavy legs into a sign of harm.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You ran this week exactly as planned, and that discipline matters more than an 80-mile week. …
Answers: (1) No. … (2) You have already seen what a big jump costs. … (3) The timing also works against you. A week of training takes two to three weeks to show up as fitness. (4) Your club mate's 70 miles took months or years to build. … (5) Doubles are also the wrong tool for a marathon. … (6) Here is what you can do instead. …
Next week:
Mon: rest. A full day off so the legs absorb Sunday's 15 miles before a bigger week.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145 bpm, then 6 x 20 s strides with a full walk back…
Wed: quality, 9 mi: 2 mi easy, then 3 x 1.5 mi at 7:55–8:05/mi with a 3 min easy jog…
Thu: easy, 9 mi, heart rate under 145 bpm, flat route if you have one. This longer run…
Fri: rest. Recovery before the weekend's key run.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 145 bpm, relaxed. A short, easy run so Sunday starts…
Sun: long, 17 mi: 12 mi easy at 9:50–10:05/mi with heart rate under 148 bpm, then 4 mi…
